entries.name: cl_c2sImpulseBackup

entries.name: cl_c2spps
entries.description:
Packet filtering (a la Qizmo's .c2spps command).
Use this to reduce network traffic if you're playing on a 28800 (or worse) connection and can't set cl_maxfps 72 because it causes lag.
Also consider use of FPS independent physics in conjunction with cl_physfps.

entries.name: cl_nolerp
entries.description:
Allows you to disable the linear interpolation (lerp) of objects in the game.
Information about objects' states arrive periodically via the net connection. By default between these moments the client tries to interpolate where the objects are. After the new packet arrives client corrects the position of the object.
If the interpolation is disabled, client will leave object in the state described in the last received packet until a new one arrives.

entries.name: cl_nolerp_on_entity
entries.description:
Disables linear interpolation only when player is standing on an entity.
It is a workaround to remove jittering of floating platforms under feets.

entries.description: Allows other protocol extensions other than Chunked downloads.

entries.name: cl_pext_serversideweapon
entries.description: When 1, requests the MVD PEXT1 server-side weapon selection extension during connect; if the server does not support it, weapon scripts fall back to client-side execution.

entries.name: cl_pext_warndemos
entries.description: If set, warning will be displayed when recording a demo that is not backwards compatible with old clients.

entries.name: cl_physfps
entries.description:
Sets the amount of FPS used to communicate with the server.
This variable is used when cl_independentphysics 1 is set, and controls the FPS sent/received to/from the server.
The graphical FPS is limited by cl_maxfps (vid_vsync must be 0).

When set to 0, the current cl_maxfps value is used.
When cl_maxfps is set to 0 too, client displays as much FPS as server and data rate allows.

entries.name: cl_physfps_spectator
entries.description:
Amount of updates the client will send/receive while being spectator.
Lower values make the client smooth-out the field of view movement greatly.
entries.remarks: This can increase your ping (only) when you are a spectator.

entries.name: cl_pitchspeed
entries.description: This variable determines how fast you you turn up/down when using "+lookup" and "+lookdown".

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_delay
entries.description: Specifies the number of milliseconds to sleep between each probe. Defaults to no delay

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_enable

values.description: Do not perform a port ping probe before connecting to a server.
values.name: false

values.description: Perform a port ping probe before connecting to a server.
values.name: true

entries.description: Toggle whether a port ping probe should be performed when connecting to a server.

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_port_probes
entries.description: Lets you set how many times each port should be probed when connecting to a server.

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_probes
entries.description: Lets you set how many port ping probes that should be performed when connecting to a server.

entries.name: cl_predict_half

values.description: Full prediction of players' movement (ezQuake default)
values.name: false

entries.remarks: The new default eliminates player models' jittering when independent physics is enabled; a possible downside is larger prediction errors of modem players' movement, hence the option to revert to old behavior.

entries.name: cl_predict_players
entries.description: This toggles the prediction for other players' movement. Unless you are having problems this variable should be left at "1".

entries.name: cl_proxyaddr
entries.description: IP address of the proxy server to use while connecting to servers.
entries.remarks: This will override the /connect and /reconnect commands so that the connection is established via given proxy server.

entries.name: cl_remote_capabilities
entries.description: This variable controls which commands and variables a server is allowed to execute or set on the client. Input a comma-separated list of commands and variables to toggle access. The default values are adapted for KTX use.

entries.name: cl_restrictions
entries.description: Triggers and re/msg trigger restrictions for spectator and demoplay modes.
entries.remarks: FuhQuake always behaves as cl_restrictions 1. QW262 has cl_restrictions 1 by default.

entries.name: cl_rollalpha
entries.description: You can turn off the 'dodging' or 'rolling' effect for your own point of view while still see other player models affected by cl_rollangle.
entries.remarks: 0 disables, 1 is standard. Disabled by ruleset smackdown and smackdrive.

entries.name: cl_rollangle
entries.description: This variable controls how much your screen tilts when strafing.

entries.name: cl_rollspeed
entries.description: This variable controls how quickly you and other players straighten out after strafing.

entries.name: cl_safestrafe

values.description: Enabled (requires one stop frame between direction changes)
Sets the number of required stop frames between direction changes.

entries.description: Enables safestrafe mode in client regardless of server enforcement.
entries.remarks: Safestrafe is a serverside SOCD fairness feature that requires one or more stop frames between direction changes.

entries.name: cl_savehistory
entries.description: Save console commands history to .ezquake_history. Loads history from this file while starting ezquake.

entries.name: cl_sayfilter_coloredtext

values.description: Filter out colored and white text markup

entries.description: Allows you to filter your own outgoing messages out of markup that is used in this client to send colored text.
entries.remarks:
Colored text is not supported by some other clients. See cl_sayfilter_sendboth for compatibility mode with other clients.
If you want to filter incoming messages out of colors, use scr_coloredtext.

entries.name: cl_sayfilter_sendboth

values.description: Send only one version of the message
values.name: false

values.description: Send two versions of the message
values.name: true

entries.description: When used with cl_sayfilter_coloredtext, sends two versions of the teamplay colored messages: colored one with "#c" at the end and uncolored version of the message with "#u" at the end of the message.
entries.remarks: FuhQuake users then can use "filter #u" to see only uncolored messages, ezQuake users can set "filter #c" to see only colored messages.

entries.name: cl_shownet

values.description: Print current incoming packet size in byte.
Print information about the current in coming packet and it's size.

entries.description: This variable toggles the display of current net info.

entries.name: cl_sidespeed
entries.description:
This allows you to set your strafe speed.
Obviously this is also limited by the server, usually to "320".
entries.remarks: Sign of the value is ignored.

entries.name: cl_smartjump
entries.description: Will convert +jump commands to +moveup commands when in liquid (water, lava, slime) and in spectator mode.

entries.name: cl_solid_players
entries.description: If not set then client will not perform collision detection against other players.

entries.name: cl_startupdemo
entries.description: Demo that should be played on client's startup.

entries.name: cl_sv_packetsync
entries.description: Determines if internal server should process packets as soon as received from client.
entries.remarks:
Should only affect playing on local server, when cl_delay_packet is enabled.
Recommend to disable for older mods which fake players (frogbots) and leave enabled for KTX.

entries.name: cl_textencoding

values.description: Use UTF8 encoding (larger range of characters)

entries.description: Determines method used to encoding non-standard characters in outgoing messages.

entries.name: cl_timeout
entries.description: This variable defines the timeout value in seconds until the client considers himself to be disconnected from the server.

entries.name: cl_upspeed
entries.description:
This allows you to set the speed with which you move up and down in liquids or in spectator mode.
Obviously this is also limited by the server, usually to 320*0.7 = 224 when being in liquid and to 500 in spectator mode.
entries.remarks: Sign of the value is ignored.

entries.name: cl_useimagesinfraglog
entries.description: Turns on using images in the frags tracker window to show which weapon did take the role in the frag.
entries.remarks: See Tracer Stats manual page for further info.

entries.name: cl_useproxy

values.description: do not use Qizmo to connect a server chosen in the Server Browser
values.name: false

entries.name: cl_username
entries.description: Username for server authentication. Setting this loads a matching .apikey token file and, if connected, sends a login command to the server; clearing it while logged in sends logout.

entries.name: cl_verify_qwprotocol

values.description: Do not check if client is associated with qw:// URLs
Check if client is associated, prompt if not
Always associate client with qw:// URLs

entries.description: Enables the check on client startup for handling URLs starting with qw://
entries.remarks: When enabled and the client is not associated with handling of qw:// URLs, user will be prompted if he wishes to associate the client with the protocol.

entries.name: cl_voip_capturingvol

entries.name: cl_warncmd
entries.remarks: Note: Not saved to config with cfg_save command.

entries.name: cl_warnexec

weapon/impulse command picks best weapon at the time of command, with fallback to axe or sg (see /cl_weaponhide_axe)

After you fire your weapon, it will get switched to shotgun or axe

entries.remarks: See cl_weaponhide and cl_weaponpreselect.

entries.name: cl_weaponpreselect

values.description: Weapon preselection when not holding +attack. When holding +attack, select weapon immediately.
Like option 1, but only for deathmatch mode 1, otherwise like 0.
Like option 2, but only for deathmatch mode 1, otherwise like 0.

When using the weapon command, this variable allows weapon preselection instead of standard immediate weapon selection.
Preselection means that the preselected weapon will be switch right before +attack command, that is right before you shoot from your weapon.

Usefull in most teamplay games where you don't want to carry your best weapon in your hands but want to be ready to instantly shoot from it.
Note: Doesn't work for impulse command, you have to use new weapon command.

entries.name: cl_window_caption

'bind x y' will bind y to physical key x, as if using an American keyboard layout (layout independent)

entries.name: con_hide_chat_input
entries.description: Hides the input of own chat text in the console.
entries.remarks: cl_chatmode must be 1 or 2.

entries.name: con_highlight

values.description: Highlighted line will be all white.
Highlighted line will start with the text given in con_highlight_mark
Both 1 and 2: highlighted line will be white and start with special text

entries.description: Console highlighting mode. Will highlight a line in the console which contains your nickname.
entries.remarks: See con_highlight_mark.

entries.name: con_highlight_mark

values.description: This text will be used on the beginning of the highlighted line

entries.description: Specifies the text that will be used to highlight lines with con_highlight 2 and 3.

entries.name: con_margin_left
entries.description: If set, messages are padded on the left by the number of spaces defined in the variable

entries.name: con_mm2_only
entries.description: If set, notification area is limited to mm2 (/say_team) messages.

entries.name: con_notify
entries.description: Toggles the display of the notification area.
entries.remarks: Notification area is the place where chat and game messages are displayed.

entries.name: con_notifylines
entries.description: This variable sets the maximum number of notify lines (default 4, max 15) to be used at the top of the screen.
entries.remarks: Only affects con_notify.

entries.name: con_notifytime
entries.description: How long console messages stay on screen.

entries.name: con_prompt_charcode

entries.name: con_shift

entries.name: con_tilde_mode

Treat tilde as a key leading to typing the character associated with it (tilde does not close the console)
Same as 1, but tilde does close the console if the console is empty

entries.remarks: To exit the console with con_tilde_mode 1, use Escape.

entries.name: con_timestamps
entries.description: Toggles time stamps before mm1 or spectator messages. Does not apply to messages with cl_fakename.

entries.name: coop
entries.description:
Whether the next "map" command should start a coop (cooperative) game.
Only works when deathmatch var is 0, otherwise coop will be forced off and a deathmatch game will start.

You need a file, spprogs.dat, in your quake/qw/ folder for coop games to work.

entries.name: crosshairalpha
entries.description: This command regulates crosshair transparency, you can use any value from "0" to "1".

entries.name: crosshaircolor
entries.description: This variable defines the color of the crosshair.

entries.name: crosshairimage
entries.description: The filename of the crosshair image.
entries.remarks: Crosshair images should be placed in ./ezquake/crosshairs or ./qw/crosshairs directory.

entries.name: crosshairscale
entries.description: When using built-in crosshairs, increases the resolution of the crosshair, giving a crisper image on screen.
entries.remarks: Max value 5. Increasing this value will require lowering of /crosshairsize to give same size image on screen.

entries.name: crosshairscalemethod
entries.description: Determines how crosshair images are scaled.
entries.remarks: When changing this value, /crosshairscale & /crosshairsize should be adjusted accordingly.

entries.name: crosshairsize
entries.description: Performs basic scaling of the crosshair.
entries.remarks: Maximum value 20. For example, /crosshairsize 0.5 halves the size, and /crosshair 2 doubles it.

entries.name: cvar_viewdefault
entries.description: When you type a cvar name into console (like 'gl_gamma' or 'r_rocketlight'), the client will tell you the default value of the cvar.

entries.name: cvar_viewhelp
entries.description: Automatically prints manual page when a variable name is typed in the console.

entries.name: cvar_viewlatched
entries.description: When you type a variable name in the console, you'll be able to see it's latched value if this is turned on.
entries.remarks: Latched values are used for example for renderer settings. Variable value is latched until the renderer is restarted, in that moment the latched value becomes the actuall value of the variable.

entries.name: deathmatch

Arena mode: players have all weapons and full health/armor

entries.name: default_fov
entries.description:
Very useful in TeamFortress, and other mods that reset your fov when you spawn to 90.
Basically, when the server sends you "fov 90", your fov is set to default_fov.

entries.name: demo_autotrack
entries.description: Enables server-side autotrack to be accepted.
entries.remarks: Server-side autotrack is recorded in MVD demos and in QTV stream allowing all the observers of the match observe the same player at the same time.

entries.name: demo_benchmarkdumps
entries.description:
Allows you to automatically dump timedemo benchmark results into $log_dir/timedemo.log file.
The output is in XML markup format and contains info about your operating system, hardware configuration, client version, rendering, screen resolution and the result FPS.
entries.remarks:
See timedemo command description for more info.
Note: The result file is not a well-formed XML file.

entries.name: demo_capture_background_threads

Note that this would typically be scaled up when using a monitor with widescreen aspect ratio.

entries.name: fraglimit
entries.description: Amount of frags any player has to reach before the match is over.
entries.remarks: When set to 0, there won't be any limit.

entries.name: freelook

values.description: Both -mlook and freelook 0 must be specified to disable free look mode.
values.name: false

values.description: Enables free look mode, that is, moving the mouse forward and back moves your view
values.name: true

entries.remarks: direction up or down.

entries.name: fs_cache
entries.description: Enables Quake File System caching of files lists.

entries.name: fs_savegame_home
entries.description: When enabled (default), save games are written under the ezQuake home directory: `~/.ezquake/<gamedir>/save/` on Linux/macOS, `Documents\ezQuake\<gamedir>\save\` on Windows. When disabled, saves go to the game directory alongside the pak files.

entries.name: gender
entries.description: Indicates the gender of the player.
entries.remarks: This relies on server/mod support to function correctly.

entries.name: gl_alphafont

values.description: Use only 2 levels of transparency for console font
values.name: false

values.description: Use full 256 levels of transparency for console font
values.name: true

entries.description: Allows alpha transparency layer support for the console font.

entries.name: gl_anisotropy

values.description: 0 and 1 means turned off, then usually up to 16 for the highest quality.

entries.description: Anisotropic filtering. Improves texture detail on angled surfaces.
entries.remarks: Depends on your Graphics card capabilities and settings. Make sure you have set your graphic card's Anisotropic Filtering setting to "Application controlled".

entries.name: gl_bounceparticles
entries.description: Controls whether sparks bounce off walls.
entries.remarks: Bouncing particles look nicer, but may eat up CPU.

entries.name: gl_brush_polygonoffset
entries.description: Offset drawing of entity models to stop z-fighting.
entries.remarks: Disabled for qcon (can cause flickering areas, most often on Intel cards).

entries.name: gl_brush_polygonoffset_factor
entries.description: Set the factor for gl_brush_polygonoffset. Negative values offset the brushes towards the player.

entries.name: gl_buildingsparks
entries.description: Buildings that are destroyed in TF will continue to throw sparks until they disappear.

entries.name: gl_caustics
entries.description: Enable reflections in submerged areas (under water, lava, slime).
entries.remarks: Multi-texturing is required for this setting.

entries.name: gl_charsets_min

values.description: Search for full range of unicode charsets
values.name: false

values.description: Search for default and -cyr only (as per ezQuake 2.2)
values.name: true

entries.description: Speeds up start-up time by only searching for minimum number of charsets during start-up.

entries.name: gl_clear
entries.description:
Clears the screen with gl_clearcolor between each frame.
Prevents hall-of-mirrors glitches, e.g. when flying out of the map.
entries.remarks: This can cause problems when going through the surface of a liquid, as you may see a colored flash where the liquid texture would normally glitch.

entries.name: gl_clearColor
entries.description: Sets clear color (gl_clear 1).
entries.remarks: When using vid_framebuffer, the GPU starts from a clean, black buffer and this value is effectively ignored.

entries.name: gl_clipparticles
entries.description: Limits the number of blended particles close to you. This can give a big FPS increase when blended particles take up a big proportion of your screen and challenge your video card's fillrate.

entries.name: gl_colorlights
entries.description: Toggles color on lighting from glowing items (quad, pent, flags in TF, etc).
entries.remarks: This implementation does not give a speed increase when gl_colorlights is set to 0, but it does not require a map restart for changes to take effect.

entries.name: gl_consolefont
entries.description:
Changes your console font.
Put all your charset images in qw/textures/charsets/*.png (and *.tga).
"/gl_consolefont original" will restore the 8bit font in your gfx.wad.
entries.remarks: loadcharset is an alias for gl_consolefont.

entries.name: gl_contrast
entries.description: Change contrast.

entries.name: gl_coronas
entries.description:
Adds coronas to some effects:

 - Explosions: Basically just a bright flash since the default explosions didn't feel powerful enough.
 - Weapon impacts (optional, see gl_particle_*).
 - Muzzleflashes.
 - Lightning bolts.
 - Fire: Torches have glows.
 - Rocket Lights.

entries.name: gl_coronas_tele
entries.description: Adds a blue glow to spawn/teleport effects.
entries.remarks: Requires gl_coronas 1.

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent
entries.description: This variable sets the percentage value for palette shifting effects (damage flash, powerup blend). (needs gl_polyblend 1).

entries.name: gl_custom_grenade_color
entries.description: Allows color of grenades to be set without requiring a texture change.
entries.remarks:
Leave blank to disable.
See gl_custom_grenade_fullbright.

entries.name: gl_custom_grenade_fullbright
entries.description: Determines if gl_custom_grenade_color refers to a fullbright color or standard.
entries.remarks: Has no effect if gl_custom_grenade_color is blank.

entries.name: gl_custom_grenade_tf
entries.description: Allows gl_custom_grenade_* variables to be ignored when playing Team Fortress.

entries.name: gl_custom_lg_color
entries.description: Allows color of lightning shaft to be set without requiring a texture change.
entries.remarks:
Leave blank to disable.
Has no effect if particle shaft is enabled.

entries.name: gl_custom_lg_fullbright
entries.description: Determines if gl_custom_lg_color refers to a fullbright color or standard.
entries.remarks: Has no effect if gl_custom_lg_color is blank.

entries.name: gl_custom_lgpack_color
entries.description: Color lightning gun backpacks with this value.
entries.remarks: Leave blank to disable. QTV/MVD only, KTX 1.38+ only.

entries.name: gl_custom_rlpack_color
entries.description: Tints rocket launcher backpacks with this value.
entries.remarks: Leave blank to disable. QTV/MVD only, KTX 1.38+ only.

entries.name: gl_custom_rocket_color
entries.description: Allows color of rockets to be set without requiring a texture change.
entries.remarks:
Leave blank to disable.
See gl_custom_rocket_fullbright.

entries.name: gl_custom_rocket_fullbright
entries.description: Determines if gl_custom_rocket_color refers to a fullbright color or standard.
entries.remarks: Has no effect if gl_custom_rocket_color is blank.

entries.name: gl_custom_spike_color
entries.description: Allows color of spikes/nails to be set without requiring a texture change.
entries.remarks:
Leave blank to disable.
See gl_custom_spike_fullbright.

entries.name: gl_custom_spike_fullbright
entries.description: Determines if gl_custom_spike_color refers to a fullbright color or standard.
entries.remarks: Has no effect if gl_custom_spike_color is blank.

entries.name: gl_cutf_tesla_effect
entries.description: When a shambler is preparing to throw lightning, or a tesla coil (TF) is charging to fire, a particle effect is generated.

entries.name: gl_detail
entries.description: Toggles an extra layer of fine detail over world textures.
entries.remarks: Can impact performance on weak GPUs.

entries.name: gl_detpacklights
entries.description: A little green light appears on the detpack, and when the timer reaches 5, the light changes to red.
entries.remarks: gl_coronas must be turned on for this to work.

entries.name: gl_externalTextures_bmodels
entries.description: Toggles loading external 24-bit textures for non-world bsp models, i.e. health and ammo boxes.

entries.name: gl_externalTextures_world
entries.description: Toggles loading external 24-bit textures for the world, i.e. the actual map.

entries.name: gl_extratrails
entries.description:
Misc trails that appear on objects that frequently move, such as TF grenades, caltrops, etc.
Railguns in TF also leave behind unique trails.

entries.name: gl_ext_texture_compression
entries.description: Compress textures on GPUs that support it to save VRAM, at the cost of longer load times and degraded quality.
entries.remarks: No longer needed when you have many hundreds of Mb of VRAM.

entries.name: gl_fb_bmodels
entries.description: Enable "fullbright" colors on bsp models (World, health boxes, etc). Might give you a couple more fps.

entries.name: gl_fb_models
entries.description: Enable "fullbright" colors on alias models (grenades, player models, etc). Might give you a couple more fps.

entries.name: gl_finish
entries.description: Wait until OpenGL has finished working to start rendering the next frame.
entries.remarks:
In the past, this setting might have helped (or worsened) some types of graphics glitches and timing issues.
It is mostly there for compatibility reasons and best left disabled unless you have bugs, performance problems, an unusual setup (in any combination).

entries.name: gl_flashblend

values.description: A glow bubble will appear on explosions and flag/quad/pent carrier.
Same as (1), but also around rockets in the air.

entries.description: This variable affects when glow bubbles are displayed in the client. You can change the color of the rocket glow by r_rocketLightColor, the color of explosions by r_explosionLightColor, and the color of flag carriers by r_flagColor.

entries.name: gl_gamma
entries.description: Change gamma.

entries.name: gl_hwblend
entries.description: Toggles between OpenGL and Hardware palette changing.
entries.remarks: 1 can be slow on WinNT/2K.

entries.name: gl_inferno_speed
entries.description: Changes speed of gl_inferno missile trail.

entries.name: gl_inferno_trail
entries.description: Changes type of gl_inferno missile trail.

entries.name: gl_lerpimages

values.description: Worse texture quality, faster loading maps.
values.name: false

values.description: Better texture quality, slower loading maps.
values.name: true

entries.description: Improves quality of non-power of two textures, at a slight load time cost. No impact on framerates.
entries.remarks: Only applies to GPUs which do not support non-power of two textures.

entries.name: gl_lighting_color
entries.description: Alias models are effected by colored lights around them.

entries.name: gl_lighting_vertex
entries.description:
Alias models no longer have the same level of light on all sides.
This may not work correctly if colored lighting is disabled.

entries.name: gl_lightmode

values.description: Makes the map lighter, but fullbrights don't look as good. (0% overbrights)
values.name: false

values.description: Makes the map darker, but makes fullbrights stand out more (looks better). (33% overbrights)
values.name: true

entries.description:
Enables overbright lightmaps.
Brings more contrast, making world lighting look more like software Quake, and less like GLQuake.
entries.remarks: Takes effect when the map reloads.

entries.name: gl_lightning
entries.description: Toggles particle lightning beams. Glow is controlled by gl_coronas.
entries.remarks: Restricted in rulesets qcon and smackdown/drive (glow effect remains).

entries.name: gl_lightning_color
entries.description: The RGB color of particle lightning beam and sparks.

entries.name: gl_lightning_size
entries.description: Adjusts size of lightning particle beam.

entries.name: gl_lightning_sparks
entries.description: Sparks fly from walls when hit by lightning gun.

entries.name: gl_lightning_sparks_size
entries.description: Size of lightning sparks.

entries.name: gl_loadlitfiles

values.description: Load lit files & use inline colored lighting.

entries.description:
Controls when external 24-bit lighting will be used.
24-bit/colored lighting is either embedded in newer .bsp files, or loaded from external .lit files.

entries.name: gl_luma_level

values.description: e.g. value 10 makes particular pixels transparent if each color component is LESS than 10.

entries.description: Some luma textures have black non-transparent pixels. This can make them transparent.
entries.remarks: Setting this to 0 will disable the functionality. For some commonly used texture packs value 1 is necessary.

entries.name: gl_lumatextures
entries.description: Turns using luma textures (named *_luma) ON when set to 1 and allowed by server.

entries.name: gl_max_size
entries.description:
This variable determines the detail level for loaded textures.
When set to "1", the objects and walls will be textured with 1x1 pixel textures.

entries.name: gl_miptexLevel
entries.description:
Downscale textures in a way that looks like the 'd_mipcap' setting from classic software-rendered QW.
Has no effect on external 24-bit textures.

entries.name: gl_modulate
entries.description: Controls how bright the lightmap gets.

entries.name: gl_multisamples
entries.description: The number of samples used around each pixel for anti-aliasing.

entries.name: gl_nailtrail
entries.description: Adds a white trail onto nails as they fly around.
entries.remarks: This feature won't work on servers not running with sv_nailhack set to 1.

entries.name: gl_nailtrail_plasma
entries.description: Adds a blue plasma trail to nail trails.
entries.remarks: Requires gl_nailtrail 1.

entries.name: gl_nailtrail_turb
entries.description: Switches between two type of bubbles nails leave behind in water.
entries.remarks: gl_turb_trails 1 needs to be set.

entries.name: gl_no24bit
entries.description: Disables support of alternate 24-bit textures.

entries.name: gl_nocolors
entries.description: Enable top/bottom colors on 8-bit .pcx skins.

entries.name: gl_oldlitscaling
entries.description: Scales lit files the 'old' way ('makes colored areas too dark').

entries.name: gl_outline
entries.description: Controls outlining of models and map. Disallowed in qcon ruleset.
entries.remarks: World outlines require vid_framebuffer 1|2 and Modern OpenGL (vid_renderer 1). With vid_renderer 0, ruleset default and sv_cheats 1, gl_outline 2 draws outlines of every surface that is rendered.

entries.name: gl_outline_color_enemy
entries.description: Determines the outline color of enemy players. Set to "" to use the value of gl_outline_color_model.
entries.remarks: Requires vid_renderer 1

entries.name: gl_outline_color_model
entries.description: Determines the color of model outlines.
entries.remarks: Requires vid_renderer 1

entries.name: gl_outline_color_team
entries.description: Determines the outline color of friendly players. Set to "" to use the value of gl_outline_color_model.
entries.remarks: Requires vid_renderer 1

entries.name: gl_outline_color_world
entries.description: Determines the color of world outlines.

entries.name: gl_outline_scale_model
entries.description: Determines the scale of model outlines. Allows values 0 to 1 for rulesets smackdown, smackdrive and qcon, and 0 to 5 for other rulesets.
entries.remarks: Requires vid_renderer 1

entries.name: gl_outline_use_player_color
entries.description: Use the top and bottom color for drawing player outlines
entries.remarks: Requires vid_renderer 1

entries.name: gl_outline_world_depth_threshold
entries.description: Threshold for finding edges with depth values. Higher value means vanishing lines at close range. Lower value means false positives at longer range.

entries.name: gl_outline_world_normal_threshold
entries.description: Threshold for finding edges face orientation. Higher value is more edges.

entries.name: gl_part_blobs
entries.description: Determines particles used for blob explosions (EMPs).

entries.name: gl_part_blood
entries.description: Determines particles used for blood effects.

entries.name: gl_part_bloodtrails
entries.description: Determines particles used for blood trails (gibs).

entries.name: gl_part_bubble
entries.description: Advanced particles for bubbles (drowning effect).

entries.name: gl_part_detpackexplosion_fire_color
entries.description: Change color of the detpack explosion fire (TF).

entries.name: gl_part_detpackexplosion_ray_color
entries.description: Change the color of the detpack explosion rays (Team Fortress).

entries.name: gl_part_explosions
entries.description: Determines particles used for explosions.

entries.name: gl_part_gunshots
entries.description: Determines particles used for gunshots.

entries.name: gl_particle_blobs
entries.description:
Determines size of blob explosions.
If set to 0, standard non-particle explosions will be used instead.

entries.name: gl_particle_blood
entries.description:
Determines size of blood effect.
If set to 0, standard blood effect will be used instead.

entries.name: gl_particle_blood_color
entries.description: Changes color of blood particles.

entries.name: gl_particle_blood_type
entries.description: Chooses among types of blood particles.

entries.name: gl_particle_deatheffect

values.description: Death effect enabled for all corpses
Death effect for gibbed players only

entries.description: Adds extra blood effects to gibs.

entries.name: gl_particle_explosions
entries.description: Determines alternate particles for explosions.

entries.name: gl_particle_fire
entries.description:
Replaces torches with a particle flame effect.
Includes people being burnt by the pyro in TF.

entries.name: gl_particle_firecolor
entries.description: Color of the fire particles.

entries.name: gl_particle_fulldetail
entries.description: Allows full detail depth for gl_particle_* effects.
entries.remarks: Requires vid_restart.

entries.name: gl_particle_gibtrails
entries.description: Enable alternate gib trails with bright blood.
entries.remarks: Requires gl_part_trails 1.

entries.name: gl_particle_gunshots
entries.description: Enable alternate gunshot impact effects.

entries.name: gl_particle_gunshots_type
entries.description: Selects alternate gunshot impact effects.
entries.remarks: Light flashes also appear with gl_coronas 1.

entries.name: gl_particle_muzzleflash
entries.description: Adds a particle effect when monsters and other players fire a weapon.

entries.name: gl_particle_shockwaves
entries.description: Controls the volumetric shockwave for the alternate blob explosion effects (r_explosiontype 6).
entries.remarks: Requires gl_particle_explosions 1.

entries.name: gl_particle_shockwaves_flat
entries.description: Adds a flat, orange shockwave to alternate explosion effects.

entries.name: gl_particle_sparks
entries.description:
Controls particle sparks.
Trails appear more beam-like and don't look stupid when they bounce.
This applies for wizards and knights only.

entries.name: gl_particle_spikes
entries.description: Enable alternate spike impact effects.
entries.remarks: Light flashes also appear with gl_coronas 1.

entries.name: gl_particle_spikes_type
entries.description: Selects alternate spike impact effects.
entries.remarks: Light flashes also appear with gl_coronas 1.

entries.name: gl_particle_telesplash
entries.description: Enable alternative teleport effect with extra sparks.

entries.name: gl_particle_trail_detail
entries.description: Controls the level of detail on the particle lightning beams, and some types of sparks.

entries.name: gl_particle_trail_length
entries.description: X - Multiplies the length of the trail on particle trails.

entries.name: gl_particle_trail_time
entries.description: X - Multiplies the length of time the particle bounces around for.

entries.name: gl_particle_trail_type

values.description: A mist of small white pebbles.

entries.description: Changes the type of particle on alt. gunshots, fuel rod explosions...

entries.name: gl_particle_trail_width
entries.description: Changes width of particle trails, e.g. wall hit by nail, explosion particles trail, etc.

entries.name: gl_part_inferno
entries.description: Determines particles used for pyro flames in TF.

entries.name: gl_part_lavasplash
entries.description: Determines particles used for lava splashes (Spy Gren).

entries.name: gl_part_spikes
entries.description: Determines particles used for spikes (nailgun etc).

entries.name: gl_part_telesplash
entries.description: Determines particles used for teleport effects.

entries.name: gl_part_tracer1_color

values.description: "R G B" format accepted, e.g. "255 255 0" for yellow

entries.description: Changes the color of the tracer1 trail, which allows you to customize the rockettrail color (see remarks).
entries.remarks: If you set r_rockettrail 6 and gl_part_trails 1, this variable will change your rockettrail color.

entries.name: gl_part_tracer1_size
entries.description: Changes the size of the tracer1 trail, which allows you to customize the rockettrail size (see remarks).
entries.remarks: If you set r_rockettrail 6 and gl_part_trails 1, this variable will change your rockettrail size.

entries.name: gl_part_tracer1_time
entries.description: Changes the duration of the tracer1 trail, which allows you to customize the rockettrail (see remarks).
entries.remarks: If you set r_rockettrail 6 and gl_part_trails 1, this variable will change your rockettrail duration.

entries.name: gl_part_tracer2_color

values.description: "R G B" format accepted, e.g. "255 255 0" for yellow

entries.description: Changes the color of the tracer2 trail, which allows you to customize the rockettrail color (see remarks).
entries.remarks: If you set r_rockettrail 7 and gl_part_trails 1, this variable will change your rockettrail color.

entries.name: gl_part_tracer2_size
entries.description: Changes the size of the tracer2 trail, which allows you to customize the rockettrail size (see remarks).
entries.remarks: If you set r_rockettrail 7 and gl_part_trails 1, this variable will change your rockettrail size.

entries.name: gl_part_tracer2_time
entries.description: Changes the duration of the tracer2 trail, which allows you to customize the rockettrail (see remarks).
entries.remarks: If you set r_rockettrail 7 and gl_part_trails 1, this variable will change your rockettrail duration.

entries.name: gl_part_trails
entries.description: Determines particles used for (rocket etc) trails.

entries.name: gl_picmip
entries.description: Determines the level of detail for world textures.
entries.remarks: Does not apply to models, liquids, simple icons, but you can also picmip these with the gl_playermip and gl_scale* cvars.

entries.name: gl_playermip
entries.description: Determines the level of detail of player model textures.

entries.name: gl_polyblend
entries.description:
Controls a short burst of screen tinting when submerged, taking a powerup, or taking damage.
Variables to look at are: gl_cshiftpercent (controls overall palette shifting) v_damagechisft v_quadcshift v_pentcshift v_ringcshift v_suitcshift.

entries.name: gl_powerupshells
entries.description: Enables a flashing layer over players carrying powerups.

entries.name: gl_powerupshells_base1level
entries.description: Baseline color level for the first powerup-shell layer (0-1, default 0.05). Adds a faint floor to all color channels regardless of which powerup is active.

entries.name: gl_powerupshells_base2level
entries.description: Baseline color level for the second powerup-shell layer (0-1, default 0.1). See gl_powerupshells_base1level.

entries.name: gl_powerupshells_effect1level
entries.description: Color intensity for the first powerup-shell layer (0-1, default 0.75). Higher values make the powerup's color more saturated (e.g., blue for Quad, red for Pentagram).

entries.name: gl_powerupshells_effect2level
entries.description: Color intensity for the second powerup-shell layer (0-1, default 0.4). See gl_powerupshells_effect1level.

entries.name: gl_program_aliasmodels
entries.description: Determines if GLSL will be used to render aliasmodels.
entries.remarks: Applies to classic OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_program_hud
entries.description: Determines if GLSL will be used to render the HUD.
entries.remarks: Applies to classic OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_program_sky
entries.description:
Determines if GLSL will be used to render skybox/skydome surfaces.
r_fastsky does not use this setting.
entries.remarks: Applies to classic OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_program_sprites
entries.description: Determines if GLSL will be used to render sprites.
entries.remarks: Applies to classic OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_program_turbsurfaces
entries.description:
Determines if GLSL will be used to render 'liquid' surfaces.
r_fastturb does not use this setting.
entries.remarks: Applies to classic OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_program_world
entries.description: Determines if GLSL will be used to render world surfaces (walls, floors..).
entries.remarks: Applies to classic OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_rl_globe

values.description: Rocket light looks like with gl_flashblend 2, but no dynamic lighting
Rocket light looks like with gl_flashblend 0 or 1
Rocket light looks like with gl_flashblend 2, with dynamic lighting

entries.description: Helps customize rocket light independent of gl_flashblend.

entries.name: gl_scaleAlphaTextures
entries.description: Applies picmip/max_size/miptexlevel to alpha masked textures (fence).

entries.name: gl_scaleModelSimpleTextures
entries.description: Applies picmip/max_size/miptexlevel to gl_simpleitem icons.

entries.name: gl_scaleModelTextures
entries.description: Applies picmip/max_size/miptexlevel to model textures.

entries.name: gl_scaleskytextures
entries.description: Applies picmip/max_size/miptexlevel to sky textures (skydome and skybox).

entries.name: gl_scaleTurbTextures
entries.description: Applies picmip/max_size/miptexlevel to turb textures (lava, water, slime, teleports).

entries.name: gl_shaftlight
entries.description: Toggles between darker/fullbright shaft beams.

entries.name: gl_simpleitems
entries.description: Toggles drawing simple icons instead of 3D item models.

entries.name: gl_simpleitems_size
entries.description: Size of simple items. Max size 16.

entries.name: gl_smoothmodels
entries.description: Toggles between flat-shaded and smooth shaded models.
entries.remarks: Applies to GLSL OpenGL renderer only.

entries.name: gl_spec_xray
entries.description: See players through walls (demo/qtv only). Is affected by gl_outline_* values like color, scale, etc.
entries.remarks: Requires vid_renderer 1

entries.name: gl_spec_xray_distance
entries.description: Distance from which you can see the players through walls, see gl_spec_xray

entries.name: gl_squareparticles
entries.description: Toggles between circle and square particles.

entries.name: gl_subdivide_size
entries.description:
This variable sets the division value for the sky brushes.
The higher the value the better the performance, but the smoothness of the sky suffers.

entries.name: gl_surface_lava
entries.description: Adds boiling bubbles over the lava.

entries.name: gl_surface_slime
entries.description: Adds bubbles and fumes of slime over the slime.

entries.name: gl_textureless

values.description: Use flat colors based on the world textures.
values.name: true

entries.description:
Toggles between textures and flat colors based on the textures (looks like gl_max_size 1).
For custom colors, look for r_drawflat.
entries.remarks:
The effect varies with picmip/max_size.
Can not be changed during a match.

entries.name: gl_texturemode

values.description: Trilinear interpolation. Highest quality, lowest performance.
values.name: GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR

values.description: Point sampled (software-like). Lowest quality, highest performance.
values.name: GL_NEAREST

values.description: GL_NEAREST but with even more quality for far objects.
values.name: GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR

values.description: GL_NEAREST but with a bit more quality for far objects.
values.name: GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST

entries.remarks: GL_NEAREST* modes are often used with gl_miptexlevel 3.

entries.name: gl_texturemode_viewmodels

values.description: Trilinear interpolation. Highest quality, lowest performance.
values.name: GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR

values.description: Point sampled (software-like). Lowest quality, highest performance.
values.name: GL_NEAREST

values.description: GL_NEAREST but with even more quality for far objects.
values.name: GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR

values.description: GL_NEAREST but with a bit more quality for far objects.
values.name: GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST

entries.remarks: GL_NEAREST* modes are often used with gl_miptexlevel 3.

entries.name: gl_triplebuffer
entries.description: Triple buffering of HUD graphics. If you have problems with screen graphics, turn this on.
entries.remarks: This has nothing to do with 3D rendering, it will not increase graphics "lag" or anything like that. It only affects 2D HUD graphics.

entries.name: gl_turbalpha
entries.description:
This variable determines the level of opacity for liquids, which requires the use of maps that were VISed with transparent water.
When using maps that have not been VISed in such a way, you have to use "r_novis 1".
If "r_novis" is set to "1" or when using a map VISed with transparent water and using setting "gl_turbalpha" to a value lower than "1", the player will be able to see objects and walls through liquids if the server allows that.
This is a very nice feature to have in the game, for more information refer to the "r_novis" command.

entries.name: lookstrafe
entries.description:
This variable toggles the automatic strafing when the +klook command is used.
When set to "1" and the player used the +klook command, the keys that are bound to the +left and +right commands will now act as if they were bound to +moveleft and +moveright.
This command was put it in order to allow keyboard player to combine the +strafe and +klook commands into one.
This command also has effect on the mouse controls. When set to "1" moving the mouse left and right will make the player move left and right instead of making him turn left and right.

entries.name: m_accel
entries.description:
Values >0 will amplify mouse movement proportional to velocity.
Small values have great effect.
entries.remarks: A lot of good Quake Live players use around the 0.1-0.2 mark, but this depends on your mouse CPI and polling rate.

entries.name: m_accel_offset
entries.description:
Acceleration will not be active until the mouse movement exceeds this speed (counts per millisecond).
Negative values are supported, which has the effect of causing higher rates of acceleration to happen at lower velocities.

entries.name: m_accel_power
entries.description:
Values 1 or below are dumb.
2 is linear and the default.
Above 2 begins to amplify exponentially and you will get more acceleration at higher velocities. Great if you want low accel for slow movements, and high accel for fast movements. Good in combination with a sensitivity cap (m_accel_senscap)

entries.name: m_accel_senscap
entries.description: Sets an upper limit on the amplified mouse movement. Great for tuning acceleration around lower velocities while still remaining in control of fast motion such as flicking.

entries.name: m_filter
entries.description:
This variable toggles mouse input filtering.
When set to "1", the values which are received from the mouse's input will first be averaged together and then that value will be used in the game.
The reason for this command is that some mice had problems with sending sporadic coordinates which make the input from the mouse jerky, also when using a serial or PS/2 mouse, the Windows operating system will only sample mouse input every 25ms, that is 40 times a second (for USB mice the sample rate is 125 Hz, that is every 8 ms).
When set to "1" this variable will smooth out the input but it will cause latency between the movement of the mouse and the actual response in the game.
When using a PS/2 mouse it is thus first recommended to try to increase the sampling rate either by changing it via your mouse driver or by using the ps2rate program which can be downloaded at ps2rate homepage.
If you are playing the game at frame rates above 40 FPS and if you can't increase the sampling rate of your PS/2 rate or if you are playing with a serial mouse it is recommended that you enable this toggle.

entries.name: m_forward
entries.description:
This variable controls how fast the player should move forward and back when the mouse is moved forward and back.
This command has no effect if the +mlook command is in effect because when the mouse is moved forward and back the player looks up and down instead of moving forward and back.
Some players might want to set this variable to "0" if they happen not to use +mlook constantly and they only want to use the mouse to turn the player.
Setting this variable to "0" will prevent the inadvertent movement of the player forward and back while trying to make precise turns with the mouse.

entries.name: m_pitch
entries.description:
This variable sets the level of precision when the mouse is used to make the player look up and down while the +mlook command is in effect.
By default this variable is set in such a way that moving the mouse forward makes the player look up and moving the mouse backward makes the player look down.
Some people prefer to have this movement inverted just like it is inverted for airplane controls.
If you wish to use this inverted mouse movement then you should set this variable to a negative value (for example "-0.022"). It is a matter of preference which movement method is used by players.
Also lowering the value for this variable will increase the level of precision when the mouse is used to make the player look up and down.
This variable can be used separately from the sensitivity variable to provide greater control over the mouse sensitivity for movement along the pitch. It is advisable to keep the value for this variable constant at 0.022 or -0.022 and instead use the sensitivity variable to change the overall sensitivity of the mouse.
Also, some script writers lower the value for this variable along with a lowered value for the fov variable in order to provide more precision when the fov variable is used to zoom.

entries.description:
Enables balancing of the buffer length of the QTV stream.
When turned on, the size of the stream buffer (the delay from the actual action) will be auto-adjusted (by changing the playback speed when necessary) so that it stays on the same level most of the time.
entries.remarks:
When turned on, the speed of the playback may change sometimes - that's how the buffer length is balanced. But usually you want to have this turned on when you are watching a shoutcast-commentated game because you want to stay synchronized with the commentary.
See qtv_buffer hud element for monitoring.

entries.name: r_netgraph
entries.description:
Netgraph is a diagnostic tool to help you tweak your rate.
If you find that you suffer from short pauses in the game and you see red spikes in your netgraph, you should try setting the rate down a bit.
The height of the pink lines towards the bottom is your latency on received packets.
Red lines are lost packets. (bad)
Yellow lines are from the rate command kicking in, it's data that wasn't sent to you because you didn't have the bandwidth for it. (OK)
Blue lines are very bad, they invalid delta's, and are related to the U_REMOVE warnings.
entries.remarks: If during your play, you frequently see a string of messages with the term "U_REMOVE" in them, and your play seems to freeze for serveral seconds, use the console command cl_nodelta 1. This is a slightly less efficient way for QuakeWorld to work, but if your ISP is overloaded or has some configuration problems, it may not pass packets to QuakeWorld properly and cause difficulty.

values.description: Calculate VIS information for unVISed maps.

entries.description:
This variable toggles the use of VIS information from the map data.
When this variable is set to "1" the game will calculate it's own VIS information on the fly instead of using the information stored in the map data, this will cause a severe performance penalty in the game.
When "r_novis" is set to "1", the variable "gl_turbalpha" has a value lower than "1" and the server allows the client to display liquid transparently the player will be able to see through liquids.
This is a nice effect to see but it is not recommended to keep this variable set to "1" because of the huge performance penalty.
It is possible to enable transparent liquids and still keep this variable set to "0" (and thus not experience such a severe performance drop) by using maps that are VISed accordingly.
You can visit the official Water VIS site at "http://www.sod.net/" and download the vispatch program along with the patch data files which you would use to update the VIS data for all of your game maps.
There are also map packs available that contain VISed versions of the original ID maps.

entries.name: sb_info_filter

Values are regular expressions, if the server doesn't have that key specified then the rule is skipped

Default (if no rules match) is opposite of the last valid rule specified.
Rules should be separated by spaces
Examples

-*version=QTV*        // remove QTV servers
-map=dm4              // fourier woz ere

entries.name: tp_pointpriorities

values.description: Original, default behavior. The closest object will be chosen.
values.name: false

values.description: Object with highest priority will be chosen. First items in tp_point have highest priorities.
values.name: true

entries.description: You can choose the way the client decides what object you want to point with $point macro.
entries.remarks:
Priorities of object are given in tp_point command. You have to type all objects manually in tp_point command.

Example: tp_point quad ra mh health
In this example, quad has the highest priority and $point will always return quad if quad ra mh are all in your view.

Example: tp_point all
You never know what object will be pointed because all objects get the same priority.

entries.name: tp_soundtrigger

Example:
filter #a
say_team I'm at %l ~location.wav"
say_team ~location.wav$\me: I'm at %l #a"
say_team ~location$\me: I'm at %l #a"
say_team I'm at %l ~location #a"

entries.name: v_kickpitch
entries.description:
This variable controls the distance that the screen should move up or down when the player is shot.
Most players set this variable to "0" in order to remove the screen tilting effect when they are injured by a shot.
This allows them to keep a perfect aim while being fired upon.
entries.remarks: v_kicktime must be >0 for this to take effect.

entries.name: v_kickroll
entries.description:
This variable controls the distance that the screen should roll clockwise or counter clockwise when the player is shot.
Most players set this variable to "0" in order to remove the screen tilting effect when they are injured by a shot.
This allows them to keep a perfect aim while being fired upon.
entries.remarks: v_kicktime must be >0 for this to take effect.

entries.name: v_kicktime
entries.description: This variable controls the amount of time v_kickpitch and v_kickroll take effect.

entries.name: vm_rtChecks
entries.description: Bitmask enabling runtime safety checks in the x86 JIT VM: bit 1 = stack underflow, bit 2 = opstack overflow, bit 4 = pointer bounds, bit 8 = data segment mask. Disable specific checks with care; disabling all (0) reduces safety for untrusted progs.

entries.remarks: This can go above 1, but sound will get more and more distorted.

entries.name: v_viewheight
entries.description:
New variable v_viewheight can be used to get the effect of negative/zero values 
of cl_bobcycle etc in qw 2.33.
Negative values of v_viewheight = lower viewheight, 
positive = higher.
Can't go below -7 or above 4 because that's the range you can get with qw 2.33 by exploiting the bob cycle bug.

Using v_viewheight automatically turns off weapon model bobbing (cl_bob*).

entries.name: watervis

values.description: GLQuake users can see through liquids if they set gl_turbalpha to a value < 1.
values.name: true

entries.description: This server-side cvar is mirrored to serverinfo as a hint to clients on whether the server is using the so-called watervised maps.
entries.remarks:
It's a bad idea to use watervis 1 if the maps the server is using are not watervised.
Liquids will appear 'transparent' but you won't be able to see any items/players/etc through it.
It is a bad idea anyway because Quake maps were not designed for transparent water (or other liquids); enabling it changes gameplay, decreases fps and produces more network traffic and puts non-GL players at a disadvantage because the software renderer doesn't support transparent water (yet).
Not saved to config with cfg_save command.
